title: 4 agentic AI interview questions, with model answers
caption:
Most agent interviews don't ask you to recite a framework. They ask how you recover when a tool fails, when a human must approve a write, when the tool list gets huge, and how you pick a decoding strategy.

I pulled 4 real questions from a public GitHub company-wise list (company attribution unverified) and wrote our model answers: what the interviewer is checking, plus a strong outline.

Exact questions:
1) How do you handle tool-call errors, timeouts and retries in an agentic loop?
2) Design human-in-the-loop approval for an agent that takes consequential actions.
3) How many tools is too many? How do you design tool schemas an LLM can actually use correctly?
4) Compare greedy, beam search, top-k, top-p and temperature sampling. When does each fail?

Which one would trip you up? Tell me in the comments, and save this before your next agent interview.

slides.title: How do you handle tool-call errors, timeouts and retries in an agentic loop?
paragraphs: Listed in a public GitHub list (**unverified**). Our model answer below.
They're checking whether you **classify failures**, not just "retry three times".
slides.callout: Retryable vs non-retryable. Budget. Escalate. Never loop forever.

slides.title: Strong outline for tool failures
items: Classify retryable vs non-retryable at the failure
Cap with a retry budget; escalate when spent
Return the error as the tool observation

slides.title: Design human-in-the-loop approval
slides.body: For an agent that takes consequential actions. (Unverified list.)
slides.after: One tool, one envelope. Gate risky tools.

cards.title: Scope per agent
cards.text: Small catalogs. Full lists burn tokens.

cards.title: Schema quality
cards.text: Tight schemas. Say when **not** to call.

cards.title: Promote to agent
cards.text: Owns retries or policy? Make it a specialist.

cards.title: Beam

cards.title: Temperature
cards.text: >0.8 gets wild; low + no sample ≈ greedy.
